channel.title: Day & Night Services — Life Insurance
channel.description: Honest, no-pressure life insurance education from Greg Jimenez, independent broker.

item.title: Your 401k is not life insurance
item.description:
One builds money for a retirement you get to see. The other replaces your income for the people who would still have bills after you are gone. Two different problems.
If no one depends on your paycheck, you may genuinely not need it. If someone would have to change their whole life without your income, it is worth a 15-minute honest conversation.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: The day you hold your first baby
item.description:
That is the moment life insurance actually starts to matter. Not because anything will happen, but because if it did, they would still be okay.
It usually costs less than people guess. A lot less.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: You just bought the house. Now what protects it?
item.description:
A mortgage is a promise that outlives a paycheck. If the income that covers it stops, the house should not be the thing your family loses.
A term policy sized to the loan is often the simplest, cheapest answer. No pressure to overbuy — just enough to keep them in the home.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: Final expense is not about you
item.description:
It is about not leaving the bill to them. A funeral runs thousands of dollars, and it lands on your family in the hardest week of their lives.
A small policy covers it so they can grieve instead of scramble. Many of these skip the medical exam entirely.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: "I think I'm already covered through work"
item.description:
Maybe you are. But work coverage usually ends the day the job does, and it is often one year of salary — not what a family actually needs.
It is worth knowing what you truly have before you count on it. I will read your current coverage with you, no charge.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: Term vs. whole life, in plain English
item.description:
Term is renting protection for the years your family needs it most — cheap, simple, expires. Whole life is owning it for life and builds cash value — costs more.
Neither is 'better.' The right one depends on who depends on you and for how long. That is the whole conversation.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: Nobody depends on your income? You may not need it
item.description:
I said it. If you are single with no kids and no one co-signed your debts, a big policy may be a waste of money right now.
I would rather tell you that for free than sell you something you do not need. When life changes, so does the answer.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: A health scare makes this harder, not impossible
item.description:
Coverage is easiest to get while you are healthy — that is just the honest truth. But even with conditions, there are options, including plans with no medical exam.
Do not assume you are uninsurable. Let's find out what you actually qualify for.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: What life insurance really costs
item.description:
Most people guess three to five times too high. A healthy 35-year-old can often cover a family for the price of a couple of dinners out a month.
You will not know your number until someone runs it honestly. That part is free.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: Changed jobs? Check two things
item.description:
First, your old 401k — it does not have to sit where you left it. Second, the life coverage you just lost when the job ended.
A rollover and a personal policy travel with you. The job does not have to own either one.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: Who is the beneficiary on your policy?
item.description:
If it still names an ex, an estate, or a minor with no trust, the money can land in the wrong hands or get stuck in probate.
It takes ten minutes to check and fix. Most people have never looked since the day they signed.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: Business owners: what happens to it without you?
item.description:
If the business depends on you, so does everyone it employs and every loan it carries. Life coverage can keep the doors open and buy your partners time.
This is not a pitch — it is a plan every owner should at least have looked at once.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: An honest word on "index" policies
item.description:
You will hear a lot of hype about tax-advantaged growth inside life insurance. Some of it is real; a lot of it is oversold.
I will walk you through where it fits and where it does not — no illustration promising a number nobody can guarantee. Straight talk only.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: The best time to set this up was before you needed it
item.description:
Nobody plans on the hard day. The whole point of doing this now is that they are covered before anything is wrong.
Fifteen minutes, honest answers, zero pressure. If you do not need it, I will say so.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: What actually happens when a claim is filed
item.description:
People picture something adversarial. Usually it is a form, a certified copy of the death certificate, and a few weeks.
The delays that do happen almost always trace back to one of two things: the beneficiary on file was out of date, or nobody in the family knew the policy existed. Both are fixable today, for free, in about ten minutes.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: If you smoke, say so on the application
item.description:
The rate is higher. That part is true and there is no way around it.
What people do not realize is that a policy issued on a false answer can be contested later, exactly when your family is least able to fight about it. An honest application at a higher rate beats a cheap policy that does not pay.
Some carriers will also look at you again after a stretch of being tobacco-free. Worth asking.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: Do not name a minor as your beneficiary
item.description:
It feels like the obvious choice. It is one of the most common expensive mistakes I see.
Insurers generally cannot pay a large sum directly to a child. It tends to go to a court-supervised arrangement until they are of age, with delays and costs nobody planned for.
There are cleaner ways to direct money to a child. Any of them beat finding this out later.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: The stay-at-home parent question
item.description:
The argument against is that they do not earn an income. That misses what would actually happen.
Childcare, transportation, the running of a household — if that person were gone, someone would be paying for all of it while grieving. That is a real number.
Not everyone needs coverage here. But 'no income' is the wrong reason to skip the question.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: Your term is ending. You have more options than you think
item.description:
Most people assume the choices are let it lapse, or start over and pay more at an older age.
Many term policies include a conversion privilege — the ability to move to permanent coverage without a new medical exam. That privilege usually has a deadline, and most people find out about it after the deadline passes.
If your term ends in the next few years, read the conversion language now.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: How much is actually enough?
item.description:
The honest answer is that it depends on what stops if your income stops.
A plain way to think about it: what is still owed, what would need to be replaced and for how long, and what one-time costs would land immediately. Add those. Subtract what is already there.
That number is usually smaller than people fear and larger than what work provides.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: Final expense and the waiting period nobody explains
item.description:
Some final expense policies pay the full benefit from day one. Others are graded — for the first couple of years, a non-accidental death returns your premiums rather than the face amount.
Neither is a scam. Graded plans exist so people with health conditions can get covered at all. But you should know which one you are buying, and it should be stated plainly before you sign.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: No-exam policies: the honest tradeoff
item.description:
Skipping the medical exam is genuinely convenient, and for some people it is the right call.
The tradeoff is usually price, or a lower maximum benefit, or both. You are paying for the insurer's uncertainty about your health.
If you are healthy and not in a hurry, the exam is usually worth the trouble. If the exam is the reason you have put this off for two years, the no-exam policy beats staying uncovered.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: The two-year window, explained straight
item.description:
Most policies have a contestability period — typically the first two years — during which the insurer can review the application if a claim comes in.
This is not a trap, and it is not a reason to avoid coverage. It is a reason to answer every question accurately the first time.
After that window, an honestly-obtained policy is very difficult to challenge.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: Divorce decrees and life insurance
item.description:
A decree requiring one parent to maintain coverage for the children is common. What is also common: nobody ever verifies the policy still exists.
Premiums lapse. Beneficiaries get changed. Years pass. The obligation is on paper and the coverage is not.
If a court order in your life mentions life insurance, confirm the policy is in force and who is actually named on it.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: Annuities solve the opposite problem
item.description:
Life insurance handles dying too soon. An annuity handles living longer than your money.
They are different tools for different fears, and they are not interchangeable. Someone with young children and a mortgage has a different problem than someone at 62 wondering whether the savings last to 90.
Worth knowing which problem you actually have before anyone sells you either one.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: When it is genuinely okay to cancel a policy
item.description:
I would rather tell you to drop coverage you do not need than keep you paying for it.
If the mortgage is gone, the kids are grown and self-supporting, and no one would have to change their life without your income — the original reason may simply have expired.
Before you cancel anything permanent, check what it has accumulated. Some policies are worth more than people assume. Ask before you surrender.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: 401k rollover: the part people miss
item.description:
When you leave a job, the old plan does not follow you. It sits there, often in whatever allocation you picked years ago and forgot.
You generally have options: leave it, move it to the new employer's plan, or roll it to an account you control. Each has real tradeoffs on fees, investment choice, and access.
The mistake is not choosing wrong. It is not choosing at all for eleven years.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: Someone just died. Here is the first call.
item.description:
Not the insurance company. Call the funeral home and ask for ten certified copies of the death certificate. Nearly every institution will want an original.
Then find the policy. Check the filing cabinet, the email archive, and the former employer's HR department — group coverage is the one people forget.
Then call the carrier. If you are in this right now and do not know where to start, call me. There is no charge for helping you find out what exists.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937
